clue.text: Change the lock

definitions.meaning: to change or swap one thing for another
a ... is a lock or tress of hair, often a false one

explanation.surface: Someone is told to replace the lock on a door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the lock' suggests a door fitting, but it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are dictionary meanings: a verb meaning swap, and a noun for a hairpiece tress.

clue.text: So lacking in shrewdness it's extraordinary

definitions.meaning: read as ..., the opposite of canny, which means shrewd
weird or beyond the ordinary

explanation.surface: Someone so naive that it seems remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: CANNY is Scottish and northern English for shrewd; the prefix UN- negates it, a playful split of a word whose real sense is eerie.
explanation.definitionFit: Its real meaning is strange or eerie, close to remarkable; the first reading is a playful split.

clue.text: Complete half the puzzle correctly

parts.note: a crossword's clues divide into acrosses and downs, so one half is the downs
done right means done correctly

explanation.surface: A solver finishes half the crossword without errors.
explanation.definitionFit: Downright as an adjective means utter or total, as in a downright lie.

clue.text: Did she wind up in the heart of England?

annotationWithheld.why: Did she wind up in the heart of England? (6): GLENDA anagrammed with one N gives ENGLAND, but no clue word cleanly supplies the N (the heart of 'wind' is IN), so the parse cannot be stated honestly
annotationWithheld.clue: Did she wind up in the heart of England?

clue.text: Next I'd been surrounded by a swarm of bees

indicators.note: the letters of I'd end up with others all round them
a swarm is a disordered mass, so the letters of bees are jumbled

parts.note: I'd written without its apostrophe gives ID

explanation.surface: Someone recounts being mobbed by bees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a swarm of' looks like part of the picture but tells you to jumble the insects' letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Beside means next to, alongside.

clue.text: The old reprobate is kidding

parts.note: a reprobate is a bad lot, so the word gives bad
the old are those advanced in years, read here as in age

explanation.surface: An elderly rascal is joking around.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase splits as BAD IN AGE: an old reprobate is someone bad in age.
explanation.definitionFit: Badinage is playful banter or teasing talk, which is what kidding means.

clue.text: Be clearly proud to give support

definitions.meaning: to swagger, walking in a way that shows pride
to brace with a structural prop

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to show their pride by backing a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Strutting is a proud swaggering walk; a strut is also a brace, and to strut is to prop up.

clue.text: The posse sent out did catch, as arranged

indicators.note: did holds or catches the other letters inside it
the posse is dispersed, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sheriff's posse was dispatched and caught its man as planned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'did catch' reads as the posse catching a fugitive, but 'did' is the container itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Disposed can mean set out or placed in order, a synonym of arranged.

clue.text: Desire merely in a malicious way

parts.note: to desire is to want
merely means only

explanation.surface: A craving that is purely spiteful.
explanation.definitionFit: Wantonly means gratuitously or with deliberate malice.

clue.text: Where you're going to make your speech?

definitions.meaning: a destination written on a letter or given to a driver
to speak formally to an audience

explanation.surface: A speaker asks where the venue is for their talk.
explanation.definitionFit: An address is a location; to address a meeting is to speak to it.

clue.text: School procession

definitions.meaning: to school is to teach or coach
a line of people or animals moving along

explanation.surface: Schoolchildren walking in a line.
explanation.definitionFit: To school is to instruct, a synonym; a train is also a long moving line, as in a camel train.

clue.text: Blast! Mother has people coming

parts.note: a dam is an animal's mother
a people is a nation

explanation.surface: A host swears at the news that their mother is bringing visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of annoyance.

clue.text: Suitable little home

definitions.meaning: fitting or appropriate
short form of apartment, a small dwelling

explanation.surface: A compact dwelling that meets your needs.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means fitting; it is also the written short form of apartment.

clue.text: Pass one the explosive device, but it's no help

parts.note: to pass something is to hand it over
I is the Roman numeral one
a cap is a small explosive charge, as in a toy gun

explanation.surface: A terrorist is handed a bomb and finds it useless.
explanation.definitionFit: A handicap is a hindrance or disadvantage, the opposite of a help.

clue.text: Wine and where to lay them down?

definitions.meaning: a white or red Bordeaux wine from the region of that name
burial plots for the dead, with a nod to laying down wine in a cellar

explanation.surface: A question about storing wine bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: Laying down wine means cellaring it, but here 'them' are bodies to be buried.
explanation.definitionFit: Graves is a Bordeaux wine district; graves are also burial places.

clue.text: That means there's a cyclist ahead, he thinks

definitions.text: That means there's a cyclist ahead
definitions.meaning: the red disc on a bicycle's rear that shows up in headlights
one who reflects or ponders

explanation.surface: A driver muses that a cyclist must be in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflector warns drivers of a bicycle; someone who reflects is a thinker.

clue.text: I stop wandering and I take on a job

indicators.note: the letters stray from their order and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drifter settles down and takes employment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' turns I STOP into POSIT; 'and' and 'take' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A position is a post or job.

clue.text: Cut said the man

indicators.note: the word is spoken, so its sound counts, not its spelling

parts.note: Hugh is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man calls out an instruction to cut.
explanation.definitionFit: To hew is to chop or cut with an axe.

clue.text: By manoeuvring gets near, while you distance yourself from

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A tactical move: getting close while appearing to back away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By manoeuvring' rearranges GETS NEAR; 'while you' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange is to alienate or set apart from someone.

clue.text: Stand waiting for the driver

parts.note: the driver is a golf club, and the stand is the small peg holding the ball before a ... shot

explanation.surface: Someone stands at a kerb waiting for a lift.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a small peg supports the ball to be struck by the driver, the longest club.

clue.text: Sees how many titles there are?

definitions.meaning: finds the total by numbering
noblemen holding a continental rank equivalent to earl

explanation.surface: Someone checking the number of honours awarded.
explanation.definitionFit: To count is to tally; counts are European noblemen, and by extension titles of nobility.

clue.text: Flying club

parts.note: an airborne mammal shares its name with the club used in cricket or baseball

explanation.definitionFit: The flying mammal and the striking club share one name.

clue.text: What Ray was caught in!

parts.note: Ray looks like a man's name but is a ray of sunshine trapped in a sheltered spot

explanation.surface: A man called Ray was caught in some trap.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital R disguises a sunbeam as a person.
explanation.definitionFit: A suntrap is a sheltered sunny place that holds the warmth of the sun's rays.

clue.text: A hand holding a transatlantic fruit

parts.note: an apple is a fruit
US, across the Atlantic from Britain

explanation.surface: Someone holds an American piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: To give someone a hand is to applaud them.
explanation.definitionFit: A hand, as in give them a big hand, means a round of clapping.

clue.text: Shoot in season

definitions.meaning: to pelt with shot
to add a spice to food

explanation.surface: A hunter shooting during the open season.
explanation.definitionFit: To pepper a target is to riddle it with shot; to pepper food is to season it.

clue.text: Got out of doing something

parts.note: reads like avoiding a task, but means gaining as a result of work

explanation.surface: Someone dodged a chore.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to gain in return for labour.

clue.text: Very good starting speed

parts.note: first means at the start
a rate is a speed

explanation.surface: Praise for a fast start in a race.
explanation.definitionFit: First-rate means excellent, of the highest class.

clue.text: Find an answer when love's amiss

indicators.note: things gone wrong, so the letters are out of order

parts.note: love's here is love is, so its letters are L, O, V, E, S

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a fix when a romance goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amiss' rearranges LOVES; 'when' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To solve is to work out the answer.

clue.text: To give food to the pet, returned

annotationWithheld.why: To give food to the pet, returned (5): CAT gives the pet, but nothing in the clue as held gives the ER (perhaps 're-turned' was printed), so the parse cannot be stated honestly
annotationWithheld.clue: To give food to the pet, returned

clue.text: Prepared but indisposed to fly around

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other

parts.note: to wing is to fly
indisposed means ill

explanation.surface: Someone ready to go but too sick to travel by air.
explanation.definitionFit: Willing means ready and prepared to do something.

clue.text: Does wander about at night, lonely

indicators.note: moving aimlessly, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: late means late in the day, at night

explanation.surface: Deer roaming at night, solitary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like a verb but is female deer; 'wander about' rearranges its letters into DESO.
explanation.definitionFit: Desolate means bleak and forlorn, alone.

clue.text: In addition, accommodating the former queen

indicators.note: one piece holds the other inside

parts.note: Anne was a British queen
ex means former

explanation.surface: An extension to house an ex-monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is a building added on, an extension.
